key_insight: Claim-level verification reduced hallucinated content by an order of magnitude, but verifier reliability remained the main bottleneck.
clinical_relevance: Guideline-grounded AI answers still require oversight because verification can miss genuine errors and correction can introduce new ones.
method: Evaluated 160 expert-approved questions across four ESC cardiology guidelines using 627 hand-verified retrieval records.
Tested a five-stage pipeline under four retrieval configurations with three independent runs.
Manually audited all 606 initially refuted claims, with additional independent judging and blinded expert review.
evidence_signal: Only 44.7–50.6% of flagged claims were genuine hallucinations; single-run recall was 35.6–41.2%, and the final genuine-error rate was 1.7% of answers.
watch_item: Pipeline convergence did not guarantee correctness: 35% of genuine final errors were introduced during correction.
paper_title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Medical Question Answering on ESC Cardiology Guidelines: Evaluation and Retrieval Optimization
